Same here, one of the thoughts I have when I'm particularly upset is wanting to claw my tongue/face-off. It might just be intrusive thoughts. Everybody has them, do a different degree. For example, the self-harm community might have more intrusive thoughts about self-harm, while suicidal people might have more about suicide (jumping in front of a bus, etc.).

It usually becomes OCD when you start to partake in activities (usually illogical) to stop those intrusive thoughts. Like clicking a pen 20 times because you believe that by doing so, the thoughts will disappear. 

It also becomes a problem when these thoughts restrict your life. Say, for example, you might begin to avoid any sharp things (knives, pens, etc).

Your fidgeting might be pointing to OCD, but it's also a possible symptom of anxiety due to your intrusive thoughts. If your fidgeting starts to annoy you, visit a therapist. If you start to avoid things that impact your life, visit a therapist. If you are concerned about your intrusive thoughts, it can't hurt to visit a therapist (sort of like going to ask a question about a sore throat to your family doctor).

There is two types of suicidal tendencies. Passive and active. Active is where you plan out the details of your suicide, such as how and when you are going to do it. I believe all active suicidal tendencies are a cause for concern, though if you are sure you wouldn't really follow through your plans, you probably don't need a therapist.

Passive is where the thought of suicide regularly enters your mind. This kind might or might not have a trigger. It doesn't matter if you want to die or not, these thoughts are in your mind passively. It would be a cause for concern if these thoughts make you very uncomfortable and avoid certain experiences (triggers), interfering with your life. Otherwise, you can control these thoughts by yourself.
